rationale:
Evidence from iteration 6 (kp 6.5, kd 0.6, 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.030 m, base_speed 1.4, ki 0.05, last_direction) is the best raced result so far at 122.66, but all 60 trials still ran off track. Oval steering_oscillation rose to 0.270 from 0.250 at kp 7.0, so lowering kp did not reduce it. Across this series, oscillation has stayed between 0.25 and 0.27 whatever the kp/kd combination, which suggests the jitter is not set mainly by kp. Oval max_error is 0.064, still above the 0.06 limit. Line losses are 1.3 on the oval, 1.6 on the s-bend and 1.0 on the slalom. Progress is 0.53, 0.28 and 0.08. The off-track limit cannot be relaxed through body_width, so control has to fix it.

Change: kd 0.6 to 0.5, with kp held at 6.5 and geometry, base_speed 1.4, ki 0.05 and last_direction unchanged. This is the step the Evaluator's plan prescribes when oscillation stays above 0.2 at kp 6.5: reduce kd toward 0.5 rather than add more damping. kd has not been reducing oscillation, so less derivative action may cut noise amplification on the sensor edges. Expected result: oval steering_oscillation falls toward 0.2 or below, and max_error stays near 0.063 or lower. The main risk is that less damping lets the robot overshoot at bend entries, which could raise max_error or line losses on the s-bend.

Hypotheses: (1) derivative action is amplifying sensor noise and edge transients, so reducing kd lowers oscillation. (2) Line losses at s-bend entries are the main limit on progress. If line losses persist at the same entries after this change, the next lever is line_loss search_left or search_right. Measurements wanted: steering_oscillation, max_error and line_loss_events per track, plus progress, rms_error and control_effort.
